chunks: So call on God with exclusive obedience, howsoever the unbelievers may dislike it.

key_terms.مُخْلِصِينَ: Sincere, making pure for God alone

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be 'mukhlisin' (sincere) in worship according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Ghafir is often linked to the concept of *Ikhlas* (sincerity), emphasizing that true devotion requires purifying the heart from all worldly motives, a principle central to the Imams' teachings on spiritual purity. The mention of the disbelievers' dislike highlights the historical context of early Muslims facing opposition for their uncompromising monotheism, reinforcing the virtue of steadfastness (*Thabat*) in faith. This directive serves as a practical guide for believers to maintain ritual and spiritual integrity even when it contradicts societal norms or political pressures.
